LESSON: READING 9.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Reading for information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 9.2.1 Reading for information, part of Strand 9 in Grade 7 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can we deduce the meaning of new words found in texts? 2. How are our indigenous communities similar to each other?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read digital and print texts and identify vocabulary related to patriotism and construction and maintenance of our roads,

2. create a personal vocabulary bank of the new words picked,

3. work collaboratively to infer the meaning of words from context and share with peers,

4. use the dictionary to find out the meaning of the words,

5. work jointly with peers to use a thesaurus and the dictionary to find synonyms and opposites of the words,

6. construct sentences using vocabulary,

7. collaborate with peers to read articles from newspapers and magazines then pick out emerging issues related to the theme. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read digital and print texts and identify vocabulary related to patriotism and construction and maintenance of our roads,
2. create a personal vocabulary bank of the new words picked,
3. work collaboratively to infer the meaning of words from context and share with peers,
4. use the dictionary to find out the meaning of the words,
5. work jointly with peers to use a thesaurus and the dictionary to find synonyms and opposites of the words,
6. construct sentences using vocabulary,
7. collaborate with peers to read articles from newspapers and magazines then pick out emerging issues related to the theme. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Reading for information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: This is developed as the learner contributes to group decision-making when

reading articles from newspapers and picking out emerging issues related to the theme.

• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner exhibits self-discipline when working jointly with peers to use a

thesaurus and dictionary to find synonyms and opposites of the words as a strategy for continuous learning.

Values:
• Social Justice: This is enhanced as the learner shares resources (thesaurus and dictionary) equitably when working

jointly with peers to find synonyms and opposites of the words.

• Responsibility: This is developed as the learner observes safety precautions when using digital devices to read texts

and identify vocabulary related to the theme.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Civic responsibility is promoted as the learner interacts with articles and picks out emerging issues related to the theme.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate vocabulary derived from the theme of nationalism to similar concepts in Social Studies.
